entries.english:
11 June 1261, Prague. Bishop Hans of Prague confirms Wok von Rosenberg's gift to Hohenfurt of the church at Wesely.

To all the faithful of Christ to whom this writing comes, Hans, by the grace of God bishop of the church of Prague, in perpetuity. Since the care of our office binds us to grant the pious wishes of the faithful, especially those which increase the merit of eternal life and the welfare of those living religiously, we have received the petition of the noble Wok de Rosenberg, marshal of Bohemia, our beloved compater, all the more favorably because we have understood that it proceeds from great devotion.

To support his new foundation, the Cistercian monastery of Altovado in our diocese, he has given to that monastery, with the consent of his noble wife Hedwig, the patronage of the church of Wezzel which he holds lawfully and peacefully. He humbly asks us to approve the gift, confirm it with our permission and by an authentic instrument secure the patronage of that church to the monastery in perpetuity. Finding this request reasonable and devout, we confirm the patronage of the church of Vezzel to the monastery of Altovado in perpetual possession by this writing, on the authority of almighty God and St. Vitus the martyr. No one may infringe this document of confirmation or rashly oppose it; anyone within our jurisdiction who presumes to do so shall know that he incurs excommunication by that very act.

Given at Prague on the third day before the Ides of June, in the third year of our episcopate. Witnesses present: Herr Witigo de Chumenowe; Herr Albert de Borschowe; Herr Bilung; Herr Jakob; Herr Hirzo; Herr Hotizlaus; Herr Nicolaus; Herr Gerbert; Herr Leopold; Benisius and his brothers; and very many others. Done in the year of the Lord 1261. The two seals once attached to this charter no longer survive.

29 June 1261, Richenowe. Agnes, widow of Pilgrim von Witlingau, gives Hohenfurt the church at Deutsch-Reichenau near Gratzen.

In the name of the holy and indivisible Trinity, amen. I, Agnes, humble handmaid of Christ, wife of the late Herr Pilgrim de Vvitigenowe, now widowed but dedicated to God, to all Christ's faithful who read this writing, in perpetuity. We shall appear before the redeemer and judge of all; if advocates are to help us there, they must necessarily precede us. These advocates are those of whom the Lord says in the Gospel: “Make friends for yourselves by means of unrighteous wealth.” Such friends are dependable and, in a day of calamity and misery, do not fail to recognize their benefactor. These are understood to be the poor; at the supreme tribunal the poor have a leading place in warding off accusations. Thus whoever has earned the intercession of Christ's poor may hope well of Christ the judge.

Seeing that none are truer poor or more certain messengers of the true Jesus to the city of Jericho than those who follow the Cistercian order, who, naked, follow the naked Lord, despise the joys of the world with their flower and long to possess heavenly things, and believing that by their prayers I shall have a share with them in the resurrection, I have given in perpetuity, with full authority, to the house called Altovado of the Cistercian order, built in honor of the blessed ever-virgin Mary by the illustrious baron Wok, marshal of the prince of Bohemia, and solemnly dedicated by the most holy Hans, bishop of Prague, and to the brothers there continually serving God and the blessed ever-virgin Mary, the church at Richenowe which has fallen to me by hereditary right. They are to possess it with every right with which it was endowed from its new foundation and dedication by the venerable Hans, bishop of Prague.

I made this solemn gift without opposition, with the consent of the more noble barons and my sons Wok and Zezimir, namely their close kinsman Herr Wok, founder of the said monastery, Herr Hoiger, paternal uncle of my said sons, Herr Bodivoi and our other blood relatives. It is for the remission of the sins of my husband Herr Pilgrim, now freed from the burden of the flesh, and of all our relatives, living and dead, those who came before us, still survive, or shall come after us, that they may enjoy peace and honor in the present and everlasting joy with the holy angels in the future, amen.

Witnesses: Otto, abbot of that monastery, into whose hands we entrusted this gift; Adam, prior of Altovado; Otto, monk and priest; Gallus, parish priest of Predal; Stlzlaus, Ritter; and very many others. Done at Richenowe on the feast of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, in the year of the Lord 1261, the fourth indiction, epact seventeen and concurrent five. To ensure that these things remain valid and unbroken, we have had this document secured with the seal of my deceased husband and of his brother Herr Hoiger, who is still living.

The invocation is written in long narrow letters, with unusually long ascenders. A slightly damaged triangular seal in white wax hangs from a parchment strip and bears a five-petalled rose. Its legend reads “P. et Hogeri de Vvitigenawe”; the initial may stand for Peregrinus or Pilgrim. See Millauer, p. 38, no. 5, and Trajer's historical and statistical description of the diocese of Budweis, p. 289.
